meta.title: E-commerce coordinator at a multi-location resort retailer
meta.industry: Resort retail, six shops and an online store
meta.blurb: Keeps the online store's products, content and orders running.

opportunities.quote: typed into Shopify by hand from the buyer's spreadsheet
opportunities.why: You read product rows in the buyer's spreadsheet and type them into Shopify by hand each week.
opportunities.firstStep: List the fields you retype and where each one comes from, then connect the two systems on one record type.
opportunities.failureMode: Field formats differ between systems, so the first runs need a person checking every record.

opportunities.quote: About 40 a day, all in my own Gmail inbox.
opportunities.why: You get a high volume of customer emails in Gmail and reply straight back to each customer.
opportunities.firstStep: Turn on the inbox summary each morning and copy its action items into your to-do list for a week.
opportunities.failureMode: Summaries miss the one message that mattered, so important senders still need a rule that flags them.

opportunities.quote: written up in the same structure each time
opportunities.why: You write descriptions in Google Docs from vendor notes using the same structure every time.
opportunities.firstStep: Save your best past document as the template and write down the three inputs that change each time.
opportunities.failureMode: Drafts read as generic when the inputs are thin, so the time moves from writing to editing.

habits.name: Grouping similar tasks
becauseTasks: Shopify: Process online orders, Update product listings, Copy new products from the buying sheet into the store
habits.firstStep: Put the tasks that use the same tool into one block on your calendar.
habits.failureMode: Blocks get booked over unless they are marked busy.

thin.taskName: Copy new products from the buying sheet into the store

rules.name: Task is in the task map
Quoted evidence appears word for word in the visitor's answers
Pattern is in the catalog and every required signal was recorded
Tool is listed on the pattern, with a working link checked within the limit
Hours figures are the ones code computed
A working-habit suggestion carries no hours unless the catalog supplies a share

transcript.question: How many products do you update in "Update product listings" in a typical week?
transcript.answer: About 30 new products a week, typed into Shopify by hand from the buyer's spreadsheet.

transcript.question: How many customer emails do you answer in "Answer customer emails" per day, and where do they come from?
transcript.answer: About 40 a day, all in my own Gmail inbox.

transcript.question: Once a product is typed in for "Update product listings", where does it go or who sees it next?
options: Saved as draft for someone to review
Goes to the buyer to check
transcript.answer: Not sure. Once I type it in Shopify by hand, I don't see it going anywhere else.

transcript.question: After you answer a customer email in "Answer customer emails", where does the reply go or who sees it next?
options: Customer, plus logged in a help system
Passed to a colleague or manager

transcript.question: For "Write product descriptions", where do the product details come from, and where do finished descriptions go?
options: From buyer's spreadsheet, pasted into Shopify
From supplier info, sent to a colleague to review
From product photos or samples, into Shopify
From a brief by marketing, back to marketing
transcript.answer: From the vendor's notes, written up in the same structure each time, then into Shopify.

transcript.question: How many descriptions do you write in "Write product descriptions" in a typical week?
transcript.answer: About 30 new products a week, so roughly 30 descriptions, though I work from the vendor's notes.
